Which Strains Make You Laugh? The Science Behind Cannabis Giggles

THC, terpenes, company and setting all play a part in the cannabis giggles. Here's what research suggests, plus classic strains people link with laughter.

By the High Society teamPublished October 24, 20268 min read

08min readMost Popular
In this article
  1. Why cannabis can turn small things hilarious
  2. THC, the endocannabinoid system and mood: what's known
  3. CBD's role, and why it doesn't add laughs on its own
  4. Terpenes and laughter: limonene, myrcene and the entourage idea
  5. Sativa or indica for laughing?
  6. Laughter is social: set, setting and shared sessions
  7. Funny weed strains: classic strains that make you laugh
  8. How format changes the giggles
  9. Frequently asked questions

Key takeaways

  • No strain can promise laughs: THC level, dose, terpenes and company all shape the giggles.
  • THC acts on CB1 receptors in the brain, while CBD isn't intoxicating and doesn't add laughs.
  • Laughter is social: researchers note we're about 30 times more likely to laugh with others than alone.
  • Keep the dose modest, since too much THC can turn giggles into anxiety.

No strain can promise laughs. Still, the strains that make you laugh tend to share a few traits: a THC-forward profile, bright citrus or sweet aromas and a reputation for upbeat, talkative effects. Just as important are your dose and the people around you. Here's what science suggests about the cannabis giggles, plus classic strains people often link with them and how format changes the experience.

Why cannabis can turn small things hilarious

You've probably seen it happen. Someone mispronounces a word, and the whole room can't stop laughing for five minutes.

THC changes how you experience the moment. According to NIDA, it can temporarily alter mood, thoughts and perceptions, including your sense of time, and it can make people feel happier or more relaxed. That may be part of why an odd detail can seem hilarious, or a familiar story can feel brand new.

It isn't everyone's experience, though. NIDA also notes that cannabis can leave some people irritable or restless, and that anxiety and panic are more common with large amounts, strong products or little experience. The giggles live in a sweet spot.

THC, the endocannabinoid system and mood: what's known

Your body runs its own cannabinoid system. The endocannabinoid system is made up of cannabinoid receptors, the body's own cannabinoid compounds, such as anandamide and 2-AG, and the enzymes that make and break them down. CB1 receptors are abundant in the brain and spinal cord.

THC acts on those CB1 receptors, which helps explain its effects on mood and perception. Researchers have learned a great deal about this system, but they haven't found a dedicated laughter switch. No one can predict from a strain name who will laugh and who won't. Our plain-English guide to the endocannabinoid system explains how it works.

CBD's role, and why it doesn't add laughs on its own

CBD is the other well-known cannabinoid, and NIDA notes that it isn't intoxicating like THC. On its own, it won't bring on the giggles.

Some people assume adding CBD changes how THC feels. A controlled trial published in 2022 tested vaporized cannabis with 10 mg of THC and different amounts of CBD, at ratios common in real products. It found no evidence that CBD changed THC's subjective or pleasurable effects. If laughs are the goal, the THC number and your dose matter far more than the CBD figure.

Terpenes and laughter: limonene, myrcene and the entourage idea

Terpenes are the aroma compounds that make a strain smell like lemons, pine or fresh earth. Many people believe they shape the high, and research is starting to test that idea, but evidence on laughter itself is thin.

  • Limonene is the bright, citrusy terpene. In mouse studies, citrus oils have shown anti-anxiety-like effects. In a small 2024 study, adults who inhaled limonene along with a high dose of THC reported feeling less anxious and paranoid than with THC alone. THC's other effects didn't change, and limonene by itself did nothing noticeable. The researchers noted that the doses they tested are unlikely in typical retail flower. Learn more about limonene.
  • Myrcene is earthy and musky, with a relaxing reputation. Much of that reputation rests on animal studies and hypotheses rather than human trials.
  • The entourage effect proposes that cannabinoids and terpenes shape the experience as a group. It's a promising idea that hasn't been proven in people. See our article on the entourage effect.

If you're hunting for limonene strains, look for terpene data on the label when it's listed, since a lemony name or aroma doesn't promise high levels. The takeaway: early research hints that limonene may take the edge off THC's anxious side, but no study shows that any terpene creates laughter.

Sativa or indica for laughing?

Sativa-leaning strains have a reputation for being social and giggly, while indica-leaning ones are known as mellow. Those reputations aren't useless, but they're unreliable, because a strain's label doesn't consistently match its chemistry, as our indica vs. sativa guide explains.

A better approach is to read the label for THC level and terpene notes. If bright, citrusy or sweet strains have made you laugh before, look for similar aromas, whatever the category says.

Notice, too, that most of the classic giggly strains below are hybrids of some kind. That alone shows how blurry the categories have become.

Laughter is social: set, setting and shared sessions

Here's the part strain lists leave out: laughter is mostly social. Researchers who study it describe laughter as a social emotion, and they note that we are 30 times more likely to laugh with someone else than on our own.

That's why the same strain can feel hilarious at a game night and quiet on a solo evening. A few things help:

  • Good company. Friends who make you laugh sober will likely still be your favorite audience.
  • A light plan. A comedy, a card game or a silly playlist gives the giggles somewhere to go.
  • A comfortable place. Familiar, private surroundings help you relax.
  • Your mood going in. Stress or fatigue can tilt the experience the other way.
  • A modest dose. Enough to lift the mood, not so much that it turns anxious.

A simple plan for a giggly night in

  1. Invite the right people. A small group of friends who already make you laugh.
  2. Pick something light. A comedy, a party game or a playlist of old favorites.
  3. Agree on a modest dose. Start lower than you think you need; you can add a little later.
  4. Set out water and snacks. Cannabis often sparks the appetite, so plan ahead.
  5. Plan the ride home. Have guests stay over or arrange a sober driver.

Funny weed strains: classic strains that make you laugh

These widely known giggly strains often come up when people talk about laughter. Think of them as examples, not promises: availability varies by store and season, and the same name can differ from one grower to the next.

How format changes the giggles

The way you take cannabis shifts both the timing and the intensity.

  • Flower in a joint or bowl acts within minutes and lets you pace yourself puff by puff, which suits slow, social hangs.
  • Vapes act within minutes and are easy to stop after a puff or two.
  • Edibles and drinks take far longer to build and last longer, so the laughs may arrive late. Start low and give it two full hours before having more.
  • High-potency products, such as concentrates and infused pre-rolls, are for experienced consumers only. Too much THC is the quickest way to turn giggles into discomfort.

If you take medications, are pregnant or have a health condition, check with your doctor before using cannabis.

If the laughs tip into too much, stop, find a calm spot, sip some water and remember that the feeling passes. Our guide to getting unhigh has more ways to come down comfortably.

Curious about a product's terpenes or how much THC it holds? The budtenders at your nearest High Society store can read a label with you. 21+ only. Please consume responsibly, and never drive after using cannabis.

Frequently asked questions

Why does weed make you laugh?

THC changes mood, perception and your sense of time, which can make small things seem funnier than usual. It acts on CB1 receptors in the brain, part of the body's endocannabinoid system. Company matters just as much, since people laugh far more with others than alone. Too much THC can work against you, though, turning giggles into anxiety.

Which terpene is linked to laughter?

Limonene, the citrus terpene, comes up most often, but no study shows it causes laughter. In a small 2024 lab study, limonene inhaled with a high THC dose lowered ratings of anxiety and paranoia without changing THC's other effects, though the doses were unlikely to come from typical flower. Myrcene has a more relaxing reputation, based largely on animal research. Read terpene notes as clues, not promises.

Does sativa make you laugh more than indica?

Not reliably. Sativa-leaning strains have a giggly, social reputation, but the label doesn't consistently predict a product's chemistry or how it will feel. THC level, terpenes, your dose and the people around you matter more. If a strain makes you laugh, note its aroma and THC level, and look for similar profiles next time.

What is the best strain for laughing?

There isn't a single one. Jack Herer, Durban Poison, Super Lemon Haze and Sunset Sherbet often come up, but the same strain can make one person laugh and another simply relax, and batches differ. A moderate dose of a strain you enjoy, shared with people who make you laugh anyway, is a smart way to begin.

What helps if I get too high?

Stop using cannabis and move somewhere calm. Sip water, have a light snack and breathe slowly; the feeling fades with time. Don't drive. If someone has chest pain, trouble breathing or can't stay awake, call 911. For other questions, Poison Control is available at 1-800-222-1222.
